payload.text:
**Short answer: the "turn it on and it connects" half is already feasible and mostly already works. The "Manic opens and searches for Bluetooth" half is not possible on iPadOS for any app, so the design has to lean on the controller's own reconnect behavior.**

**How iPadOS handles controllers.** Bluetooth game controllers are paired and connected by the system, not by the app. Apps only get the GameController framework, which tells them a controller appeared. There is no public API to pair a controller, open Bluetooth scanning, or make the iPad initiate a connection to a specific device. CoreBluetooth cannot see game controllers at all, because the system claims the HID profile. The Bluetooth usage string already in Manic's Info.plist is for Dolphin's Wii remote passthrough, not for pads.

**What already happens today.** Once a controller has been paired with the iPad once, powering it on makes the controller itself reconnect to its last host. DualSense, Xbox Series, Switch Pro and 8BitDo pads all do this, with the iPad asleep or awake. On the app side, Manic's AppDelegate starts DeltaCore's controller manager at launch, which picks up any already-connected pads and listens for connect notifications. So the sequence "open Manic, press the PS or Xbox button, play" works without any code change, provided the iPad was the last thing the controller talked to.

**Where it breaks, and the fix is hardware, not software.** The controller reconnects to its last host, so if you used it on a PS5, Switch or Mac in between, it goes there instead and you have to re-pair. The practical fixes are:

- Dedicate a controller to the iPad, which is the zero-effort answer.
- Use a pad with multiple host slots. Xbox Series controllers remember one Xbox and one Bluetooth host and switch with a double tap of the pair button. 8BitDo Pro 2 and Ultimate remember a host per mode switch position.
- Keep each pad's last host the iPad for multiplayer sessions, since this is where the Mario Party setup would bite.

**The one thing worth doing in the app.** The GameController framework has a call that asks the system to wake and reconnect already-paired wireless controllers. DeltaCore wraps it, but Manic never calls it. Calling it when the app comes to the foreground, and again when a game starts, is a few lines and is the closest an app can get to "search for Bluetooth". Expect it to be a nudge rather than a guarantee. In practice modern pads reconnect on their own, and the call mainly helps when a paired pad is on but idle. I would pair it with a small "no controller connected" hint on the play screen so the state is visible.

**What cannot be done, so nobody chases it:** no in-app pairing, no deep link into the Bluetooth settings page that survives on current iPadOS, and no Shortcuts automation that connects a controller, since Shortcuts has no "connect Bluetooth device" action for input devices.

Which controller model are you planning to use, so I can confirm its reconnect and multi-host behavior specifically?
